Mono Audio engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

US/EU indie teams conflate mono-downmix capability with storefront language. iOS Settings and App Store Connect actually separate them:

  • Mono Audio on the device — when enabled under Settings → Accessibility → Audio & Visual → Mono Audio, iOS combines left and right stereo channels into both ears so single-ear listeners hear the full mix. System accessibility behavior — outside AppLocale scope.
  • AVAudioEngine downmix & mono routing in your app — custom code that detects system Mono Audio preferences, downmixes stereo tracks, or routes combined channels through your player. Engineering inside the binary — not listing rewrite.
  • Mono Audio marketing on the product page — description paragraphs, subtitle positioning, keywords, promotional text, and screenshot overlays that tell buyers your app supports Mono Audio, stereo-to-mono, or single-ear listening workflows. Connect text fields — this page.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China storefront. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, and screenshot caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of how strongly your US listing markets Mono Audio.

An app that ships mono-downmix-aware playback in the binary and a localized China listing are both valuable — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe Mono Audio and single-ear listening on the store page, not whether your player downmixes stereo inside the app.

What Apple Mono Audio is — and what your listing may claim

Apple ships Mono Audio under Settings → Accessibility → Audio & Visual → Mono Audio. When enabled, the device combines left and right stereo channels into both ears. Western indie listings often show one or more of these surfaces on the US product page. AppLocale covers paste-ready zh-Hans copy for whichever your screenshots and description already claim:

  • Mono Audio toggle (单声道音频) — master switch that downmixes stereo into a combined channel for single-ear listening. Gallery frames may show the Audio & Visual settings branch or a "Works with Mono Audio" badge.
  • Single-ear listening workflows (单耳收听) — marketing that emphasizes hearing the full left-and-right mix when using one earbud, one hearing aid, or one side of wired headphones. Screenshot overlays often show one-ear listening demos or before/after stereo-vs-mono comparisons.
  • Channel combining (左右声道合并) — when your English listing explains that both stereo channels play through each ear so no audio information is lost for one-ear listeners. zh-Hans copy should use 左右声道合并 only when your US page already claims channel combining — not as a generic "better audio" synonym.
  • Mono-downmix-aware playback in your app — in-app audio players, podcast episodes, meditation sessions, or lesson modules that respect system Mono Audio when stereo content plays. Screenshot overlays often show mono-downmix badges on player UI or settings walkthroughs.

Your gallery may lead with a Mono Audio settings toggle on one frame and an in-app player with single-ear listening callouts on the next. zh-Hans caption lines should name the correct surface per frame — a Mono Audio toggle is not a Balance slider, not a Headphone Accommodations EQ graph, and not a Live Listen microphone badge unless that is what the screenshot shows.

Mono Audio-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Single-ear listening marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe Mono Audio in iOS Settings — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Official Settings vocabulary

Apple's zh-Hans Settings UI uses 单声道音频 for Mono Audio under 辅助功能 → 音频与视觉 (Audio & Visual). Related commerce phrasing includes 单耳收听 (single-ear listening), 左右声道合并 (left-right channel combining), and 音频与视觉 when your gallery shows the Audio & Visual settings branch — not as a standalone hub title. Listing copy should mirror that vocabulary — not generic "better sound" or medical claims.

Mono Audio vs Balance

Balance shifts volume emphasis between left and right channels — 平衡 — without downmixing stereo to mono. Mono Audio combines both channels so each ear hears the full mix — 单声道音频. zh-Hans listing copy should not imply left-right volume sliders when your English source only shows a Mono Audio toggle or stereo-to-mono player demo.

Mono Audio vs Headphone Accommodations and Spatial Audio

Headphone Accommodations covers frequency EQ and amplify soft sounds — 耳机调节. Spatial Audio covers immersive head-tracked Dolby Atmos — 空间音频. Mono Audio covers channel downmix for single-ear listeners — 单声道音频. If your English gallery shows an EQ slider graph or a 3D sound badge, do not paste Mono Audio vocabulary onto those frames.

Mono Audio vs Closed Captions and Live Caption

Closed Captions displays embedded caption tracks on media — 隐藏式字幕. Live Caption generates real-time speech subtitles — 实时字幕. Mono Audio routes combined stereo audio to ears — 单声道音频. Caption and audio-routing claims use different Connect string families.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need mono-downmix search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 单声道音频, 单耳收听, and 左右声道合并 each signal different intent from 平衡 or 耳机调节 keywords.

Caption lines vs burned-in badges

Marketing screenshot overlays you control — "Mono Audio" headlines on gallery frames showing single-ear listening demos — are separate caption fields or burned-in PNG text. See Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese for caption-field mechanics when overlays are editable in Connect.
